source.title: Communication-Efficient Distributed Training for Collaborative Flat Optima Recovery in Deep Learning

record.file_problem: Text includes the paper and supplementary material; some equations, table formatting, and figure contents are flattened, but Table 1 values are legible.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether sharpness measures track the train–validation generalization gap using Kendall rank correlations, but introduces Inverse Mean Valley rather than the magnitude-aware perturbation measure in V7.
record.gate_note: Table 1 reports correlations between the generalization gap and eight sharpness measures across single-worker and EASGD settings, with and without augmentation. Inv. MV is NA in the single-worker settings. Other training and test-error comparisons concern distributed-training methods, not a version in the claim.
record.test_reason: The study uses the flat-minima hypothesis to develop DPPF and reports correlations for related measures, but does not test V7's magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance. Normalizing each layer to unit Frobenius norm does not make the subsequent perturbations proportional to individual weight magnitudes. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the correlation finding: the authors describe Inv. MV as strongly correlated with the generalization gap and comparatively consistent across augmentation conditions in EASGD. Their overall conclusion is broader: DPPF's push mechanism prevents worker collapse, recovers wider minima, and improves test performance while reducing communication, with performance comparable to SAM.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a new worker-direction valley-width measure and compares correlations with the validation–train error gap; V7 specifies magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance.
record.method_sensitivity: Correlation results vary between single-worker and EASGD settings and between augmentation conditions; Inv. MV is only available for EASGD in the reported table.

fits_no_version.finding: On CIFAR-10, the reported entropy, fixed-box sharpness, Fisher-Rao, LPF and Hessian measures have positive single-worker correlations with the generalization gap, while their strengths and sometimes signs differ under EASGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Generalization-gap correlations of confidence, capacity and geometric measures depend on the training setup and augmentation.

fits_no_version.finding: Inv. MV has Kendall correlations of 0.616 with augmentation and 0.485 without augmentation for four-worker EASGD. Table 7 reports positive correlations across κ values from 1.5 to 4.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Worker-direction valley width after layer normalization correlates with the generalization gap in these distributed CIFAR-10 experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: DPPF improves test performance against distributed-training baselines and produces wider visualized basins; these experiments deliberately introduce a flatness-seeking regularizer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding inter-worker repulsion can improve the communication–accuracy trade-off in distributed training.

record.problems: Table 1 provides correlations but no uncertainty estimates. The Inv. MV single-worker entries are NA. The text says configurations were repeated across three seeds, but does not report uncertainty for these correlations in Table 1.
record.rows_left_out: None from Table 1; all eight measures and four settings are recorded, including the two NA entries for Inv. MV.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label held-out performance under the same architecture and recipe.
Test-error trends beyond the width required for zero training error; varying width in a pooled correlation analysis does not establish this trend.
Convolutional versus fully connected classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under matched tuning; using AdamW for ViT and SGD for CNNs provides no such comparison.
Controlled batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets; worker-count comparisons also change distributed optimization, and the batch-size sweep reports no separate performance trend.

Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. CIFAR-10 without augmentation is included, and models above 1% training error are excluded, but neither establishes the specified measure or similarly low training loss. SVHN is not studied.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Table 1's numerical values are correctly transcribed. All reported states above concern applicability to the supplied versions, not whether the correlations exist. Appendix B.1 specifies ResNet-18-based models, width multipliers 4, 6 and 8, 300 training epochs, three seeds, a training-error cutoff of 1%, and layerwise normalization. It does not establish equal training loss. No uncertainty estimates accompany the Kendall correlations.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Test error as width increases past the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Large-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.

Magnitude-aware weight perturbations; CIFAR-10 and SVHN without augmentation as specified in V7; same low training loss across the compared networks; norm- and margin-based measures specifically named in V7.
Removing memorized training examples and retraining.
